topIssues.title: contracts-bedrock: Lagoon activation bricks any chain whose genesis contracts are newer than the frozen NUT bundle
topIssues.author: jelias2
topIssues.body:
## Summary

A chain whose genesis contracts are newer than the **frozen Lagoon NUT bundle** is guaranteed to brick at Lagoon activation: the L2ProxyAdmin upgrade deposit reverts with `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed`, the interop predeploys (CrossL2Inbox `0x…0022`, L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger `0x…0023`, SuperchainETHBridge `0x…0024`) never receive implementations, ETHLiquidity is never funded, and there is no retry mechanism. The chain keeps sequencing with no halt and no alert.

This happened on the `interop-sdm` devnet (chains 420120246/420120247) at its Lagoon activation, 2026-09-29 21:00 UTC. All interop messaging on both chains now reverts with `Proxy: implementation not initialized`. Discovered ~30 minutes later only because `check-lagoon roundtrip` failed.

No node version fixes or causes this — every recent op-node, kona-node and op-supernode release (and current develop) embeds the identical frozen bundle.

## Root cause

Two design decisions collide:

1. **NUT bundles are frozen at fork-definition time.** The Lagoon bundle at `op-core/nuts/bundles/lagoon_nut_bundle.json` (go:embed'd by op-node via `nutBundleForFork`, codegen'd by kona from the same file) was frozen ~June 2026 with **L2ContractsManager 1.9.1 / SequencerFeeVault 1.6.1**. Freezing is correct: it guarantees deterministic activation bytes and stable deposit source hashes across clients, for chains whose on-chain state is *older* than the bundle — which is what production networks look like.
   - Do not confuse it with `packages/contracts-bedrock/snapshots/upgrades/current-upgrade-bundle.json` (currently LCM 1.14.0 / SFV 1.7.0) — that is the *rolling* bundle for the next fork and is not what ships for Lagoon. This confusion produced the original, wrong root cause in this issue.
2. **Genesis is generated from current contract artifacts.** The interop-sdm genesis (op-deployer 0.8.0-rc.2) has **SequencerFeeVault 1.7.0** at `0x4200…0011`. Note the trigger is the *artifact* versions, not the op-deployer binary: interop-priv-1 was deployed with op-deployer 0.7.1 and its genesis also carries SequencerFeeVault 1.7.0 — it avoids the bug only because it runs Lagoon at genesis.

At activation, `L2ContractsManager._apply()` upgrades ~20 predeploys sequentially inside one deposit tx. For each, `L2ContractsManagerUtils` runs a downgrade guard ([`upgradeTo`, src/libraries/L2ContractsManagerUtils.sol#L56-L68](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/libraries/L2ContractsManagerUtils.sol#L56-L68); [`upgradeToAndCall`, #L139-L148](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/libraries/L2ContractsManagerUtils.sol#L139-L148)):

```solidity
if (
    implementation.code.length != 0
        && SemverComp.gt(ISemver(_proxy).version(), ISemver(_implementation).version())
) {
    revert L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed(address(_proxy));
}
```

On-chain SequencerFeeVault 1.7.0 > bundle's 1.6.1 → the first fee-vault upgrade reverts the **entire** `_apply`, including the interop predeploy wiring in its `isInterop` branch. The deposits that already executed earlier in the activation block persist. Result: a permanently half-upgraded chain.

## Evidence (interop-sdm-0; interop-sdm-1 identical)

- `lagoon_time: 1790715600`; activation block **8820** (`0x2274`) contains the expected 31 deposits: L1-attributes, `setFeature(INTEROP)` → L1Block, 27 × ConditionalDeployer deploys, L2ProxyAdmin upgrade, ETHLiquidity `fund()`.
- Receipts: 29 succeeded, 2 failed — tx 29 (L2ProxyAdmin upgrade, `0xdcc91ddea2ce19ff790c296f524216a1d5fe44f99063bb17824bd47ec5401ef3`, 642k gas of 3.7M) and tx 30 (ETHLiquidity funding, consequential).
- `debug_traceTransaction` (callTracer) on tx 29: the delegatecall into the LCM at `0x82c0bb44c86bbb1620583890b2af560382aa83c8` reverts with selector `0xf8ce5d16` = `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed(address)` for `0x4200…0011`; the L2ProxyAdmin wraps it in `0x1c0a89cc` (delegatecall-failed).
- On-chain `SequencerFeeVault.version()` = **1.7.0**; on-chain LCM `version()` = **1.9.1**; the LCM's `getImplementations()` SequencerFeeVault impl reports **1.6.1**.
- Sequencer verified in-cluster: `op-node v1.19.8-rc.1-9f76a9d2`, commit matches the release tag; that commit's `op-core/nuts/bundles/lagoon_nut_bundle.json` carries LCM 1.9.1 / SFV 1.6.1 — as does develop today. The running node was exactly what the manifest pinned; version skew between op-node / kona-node / op-supernode is ruled out (all embed the same frozen file).
- Terminal state: EIP-1967 impl slots at `0x…0022/0023/0024` are zero, no code at `0xc0d3…0024`, `isFeatureEnabled(INTEROP)` = true, ETHLiquidity unfunded.

## Why this is a bug, not an ops mistake

1. **Guaranteed by construction.** A fresh chain genesis'd from any monorepo state newer than the bundle freeze, with a Lagoon transition scheduled, *always* bricks. Genesis-newer-than-frozen-bundle is the default state of every new devnet.
2. **No recovery path.** Activation fires once at the fork boundary. Removing or re-timing `lagoon_time` changes derivation, so reconfigured nodes derive a different block 8820 and split from the batches already posted to L1. A devnet can be redeployed; a long-lived chain could not.
3. **Partial terminal state.** The guard protects one fee vault by bricking interop chain-wide, while earlier deposits in the same activation block persist.
4. **Silent.** Sequencer, batcher, proposer and challenger all continued past a failed network upgrade. Nothing asserts deposit receipt statuses in activation blocks.
5. **Transition path validated only for bundle-era genesis.** The dev-preview devnets (genesis SequencerFeeVault **1.6.1**, equal to the bundle's) had `lagoon_time` in early August 2026 and show no sign of this failure — consistent with the transition working when on-chain versions ≤ bundle versions (the guard cannot trip). Their RPCs are no longer reachable, so the activation receipts were not re-verified. Production chains (contracts predating the freeze) should therefore pass, but each target's on-chain versions should be checked against the bundle before its activation rather than assumed.

## Current workarounds (new networks only)

| Goal | Setup |
|---|---|
| Interop working; don't care about the transition | Lagoon active at genesis (`l2GenesisLagoonTimeOffset: "0x0"`). The genesis deploy path (`LCM.deploy()`) applies current contracts directly; no NUT runs. Supported by op-contracts/v8.0.0 (`L2Genesis.s.sol` Fork.LAGOON + `_isGenesisInteropEnabled`), op-deployer 0.8.0-rc.2, and netchef override pass-through. **Field-validated:** interop-priv-1/2/3 and zk-proofs-1 run `lagoon_time=0`; interop-priv-1's genesis alloc has the SuperchainETHBridge impl slot pre-set to `0xc0d3…0024` *with* SequencerFeeVault 1.7.0 contracts. |
| Rehearse the Lagoon *transition* | Genesis must use pre-freeze contract artifacts (SequencerFeeVault ≤ 1.6.1, ~June 2026 era) — also the production-faithful shape. |
| Current genesis contracts + later Lagoon transition | Impossible today — this is the bug. |

## Proposed fixes

### 1. Contracts (primary): skip-on-newer in `L2ContractsManagerUtils`

When the on-chain contract is strictly newer than the bundle's implementation, reverting protects nothing — skipping that one contract downgrades nothing. Replace the revert with a skip + event in both `upgradeTo` and `upgradeToAndCall`:

```solidity
event L2ContractsManager_UpgradeSkipped(address indexed target, string onchainVersion, string bundleVersion);

function _skipAsNewer(address _proxy, address _implementation) private returns (bool) {
    address implementation = IL2ProxyAdmin(Predeploys.PROXY_ADMIN).getProxyImplementation(_proxy);
    if (implementation.code.length == 0) return false; // newly introduced predeploy
    string memory onchain = ISemver(_proxy).version();
    string memory next = ISemver(_implementation).version();
    if (!SemverComp.gt(onchain, next)) return false;
    emit L2ContractsManager_UpgradeSkipped(_proxy, onchain, next);
    return true;
}
```

Properties: deterministic (consensus-safe); skipping `upgradeToAndCall` also skips the initializer re-run, which is correct since the newer contract was already initialized; equal versions still re-upgrade and re-initialize (initializers must be idempotent per contracts-bedrock/AGENTS.md); the event gives monitoring a pageable signal for production networks where on-chain-newer *is* unexpected — it pages on a live chain instead of bricking a stuck one; the skip path is cheaper, so the bundle's fixed gas reservation still covers it. `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed` becomes unused and is removed.

**Constraint:** this must ship *inside the frozen Lagoon bundle* (new LCM creation code → new deposit source hashes), so the bundle must be regenerated and the fix must land **before Lagoon activates on any network that matters**. The window closes at first real activation. No client code changes: op-node and kona pick up the regenerated JSON together.

Alternative considered: making the whole activation atomic (deploys + upgrade in one deposit) fixes the partial state but not the no-retry brick, and is a much larger bundle-format change. Rejected.

### 2. Tooling: deploy-time gate

op-deployer / netchef must refuse to launch a network whose genesis contract versions exceed the versions in the **frozen bundle of any fork scheduled after genesis** (not the rolling current bundle). This would have made interop-sdm undeployable instead of time-bombed.

### 3. Monitoring

Alert on any failed deposit receipt in a hardfork activation block, and on `L2ContractsManager_UpgradeSkipped` once fix 1 lands.

### 4. Related cleanup

`netchef pkg/interactive_add_hardfork.go` maps `forks.Lagoon` to `interop_time`/`interopTime` config keys while generated rollup configs use `lagoon_time` — likely stale from the Interop→Lagoon rename; unverified whether any flow hits it.

## Status

- interop-sdm is unrecoverable and will be replaced by a Lagoon-at-genesis devnet (draft PR: ethereum-optimism/devnets-private#1887, chains 420120248/420120249). Post-deploy sanity check: the generated genesis.json alloc must have the EIP-1967 impl slot set for `0x4200…0024` (as interop-priv-1's does) before pointing traffic at it.
- Fix 1 draft is ready to become a PR pending contracts-team sign-off on the approach (tests: newer-on-chain → skipped + event + rest of `_apply` completes; equal → upgraded; fresh proxy → upgraded).

Related: #19239 (NUT bundle migration), #20402 (interop activation plan), #22460 (bundle intent rename).

topIssues.title: op-node: origin prefetch ordering regression on 10-second L2 chains since v1.19.5
topIssues.author: atenalt
topIssues.body:
## Summary

We observed persistent L1-origin lag on a custom OP Stack rollup with **10-second L2 blocks** after upgrading op-node to **v1.19.9**. L2 block timestamps remain fresh and derivation stays at the configured L1 confirmation distance, but the unsafe L2 head's L1 origin falls approximately 148–149 L1 blocks behind the observed L1 head, near the Fjord 1,800-second drift limit.

Source-history analysis and controlled component tests identify an ordering change introduced by **#22241 / `4c3d0d3da6`**, first included in stable **v1.19.5**: the direct sequencer path can schedule its next build before the shared event dispatcher runs the next-origin prefetch triggered by `ForkchoiceUpdateEvent`.

This report concerns origin advancement, not a failure to produce L2 blocks. We would appreciate confirmation of whether this is an unintended regression and guidance on preserving timely origin adoption without reintroducing derivation-induced sequencer starvation.

## Environment and observations

- Observed deployed version: op-node v1.19.9; execution client op-reth v2.6.0.
- L1: Sepolia, approximately 12-second blocks.
- L2 block time: 10 seconds.
- Sequencer and verifier L1 confirmations: 15.
- Consensus-layer sync; Fjord, Granite and Holocene active; Isthmus not activated.
- CPU was not saturated during this investigation.

At a representative sample:

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `head_l1.number - current_l1.number` | 15 |
| `head_l1.number - unsafe_l2.l1origin.number` | 149 |
| Unsafe L2 timestamp age | approximately 3 seconds |
| Unsafe-to-safe L2 distance | approximately 20–24 blocks |

Safe/finalized progress and L1 transaction confirmations continued. Sequencing logs repeatedly showed the same origin used for two consecutive 10-second L2 blocks, for example:

```text
L2 parent  N     -> origin O
L2 parent  N+1   -> origin O
L2 parent  N+2   -> origin O+1
L2 parent  N+3   -> origin O+1
```

Reverting **only op-node** to the previously deployed v1.17.0 restored one origin advance per L2 block while behind, and the observed head-to-origin lag began decreasing (146 → 144 → 143, later 122). Execution client, batcher, RPC provider, fork schedule and confirmation settings were unchanged. This rollback was diagnostic, **not a recommendation to run an old client after Sepolia's L1 fork**; we are aware of the v1.19.5+ requirement.

## Suspected mechanism

1. The selector has cached current origin `O` and next origin `O+1`.
2. A newly inserted L2 block adopts `O+1`.
3. The direct sequencer path completes `ProcessPayload` and calls `scheduleNextAction` without requiring the shared dispatcher to finish the corresponding forkchoice-prefetch handler.
4. If the next `FindL1Origin` runs first, `CurrentAndNextOrigin` promotes cached `O+1` to current and clears the next-origin cache.
5. With no next origin cached and drift still below its limit, the selector reuses `O+1`, despite `O+2` being available and having a valid timestamp/confirmation distance.
6. The later forkchoice handler prefetches `O+2`, but the missed adoption opportunity can repeat as origins advance.

With 10-second L2 blocks, advancing an origin only once per two L2 blocks means approximately 20 seconds per origin, slower than L1's approximately 12-second block interval. Once drift approaches the limit, the synchronous-fetch fallback constrains the lag rather than restoring the intended confirmation-distance target. Faster 2-second chains can still keep up despite the missed opportunities, so the effect is more visible with a longer L2 block time.

Relevant source:

- [Sequencer concurrency change #22241](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22241)
- [Introduction commit](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/commit/4c3d0d3da6c9b2edd9ac93756aef5629b8a97b44)
- [v1.19.9 origin selector](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/op-node/v1.19.9/op-node/rollup/sequencing/origin_selector.go)
- [v1.19.9 sequencer](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/op-node/v1.19.9/op-node/rollup/sequencing/sequencer.go)

## Controlled source-boundary tests

We tested isolated production-source snapshots with their original module pins and checksum-verified superchain bundles, using Go 1.26.6 and test-only overlays. The probes use each snapshot's **actual Sequencer and L1OriginSelector**, existing attribute/conductor test fixtures, and a mocked successful engine insertion with deliberately controlled forkchoice-dispatch timing. Each boundary test was repeated 20 times.

The setup has current origin 818, prefetched origin 819, and origin 820 already available with a valid timestamp. The inserted child adopts 819. The question is whether the next build can run before the selector handles the child's forkchoice update.

| Source snapshot | Before prefetch fanout | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `4c3d0d3^` (`20818c5b`) | Payload success alone does not arm the next build; shared forkchoice processing precedes the next action | selects 820 |
| `4c3d0d3` | Direct insertion arms the next build independently | delayed prefetch selects 819; prefetch-first control selects 820 |
| stable v1.19.4 | same as the parent | selects 820 |
| stable v1.19.5 | same as the child | delayed prefetch selects 819; prefetch-first control selects 820 |

These are **controlled component tests, not an end-to-end historical-binary/network bisect**. They reproduce the call-site ordering change; the production v1.19.9 versus node-only rollback comparison provides separate operational evidence. Tests with Isthmus disabled and enabled both reproduced the same origin-selection outcome.

### Minimal selector-order reproducer

The following self-contained program models the triggering event order using the real selector. Run it from an upstream module checkout, for example v1.19.5, with its normal dependencies available:

```bash
go run /tmp/origin-order-repro.go
```

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "log/slog"
    "math/big"

    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-node/rollup"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-node/rollup/engine"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-node/rollup/sequencing"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/eth"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/common"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/log"
)

type source struct {
    sequencing.L1Blocks // Unused additional methods, if present, must not be called.
    now uint64
}

func block(n uint64) eth.L1BlockRef {
    return eth.L1BlockRef{
        Number: n, Time: n * 12,
        Hash: common.BigToHash(new(big.Int).SetUint64(n)),
        ParentHash: common.BigToHash(new(big.Int).SetUint64(n - 1)),
    }
}

func (s *source) L1BlockRefByNumber(_ context.Context, n uint64) (eth.L1BlockRef, error) {
    if n + 15 > s.now / 12 {
        return eth.L1BlockRef{}, ethereum.NotFound
    }
    return block(n), nil
}

func (s *source) L1BlockRefByHash(_ context.Context, h common.Hash) (eth.L1BlockRef, error) {
    return block(h.Big().Uint64()), nil
}

func run(prefetchFirst bool, blockTime uint64) {
    ctx := context.Background()
    src := &source{now: 10000}
    cfg := &rollup.Config{BlockTime: blockTime, MaxSequencerDrift: 1800}
    logger := log.NewLogger(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil))
    sel := sequencing.NewL1OriginSelector(ctx, logger, cfg, src)
    head := eth.L2BlockRef{Number: 100, Time: src.now, L1Origin: block(src.now/12 - 15).ID()}
    for i := 0; i < 600; i++ {
        src.now = head.Time
        ev := engine.ForkchoiceUpdateEvent{UnsafeL2Head: head}
        if prefetchFirst { sel.OnEvent(ctx, ev) }
        origin, err := sel.FindL1Origin(ctx, head)
        if err != nil { panic(err) }
        if !prefetchFirst { sel.OnEvent(ctx, ev) }
        head = eth.L2BlockRef{Number: head.Number + 1, Time: head.Time + blockTime, L1Origin: origin.ID()}
    }
    fmt.Printf("prefetchFirst=%v blockTime=%d originLag=%d drift=%d\n",
        prefetchFirst, blockTime, head.Time/12-head.L1Origin.Number,
        head.Time-block(head.L1Origin.Number).Time)
}

func main() {
    run(true, 10)
    run(false, 10)
    run(false, 2)
}
```

Observed output:

```text
prefetchFirst=true  blockTime=10 originLag=16  drift=196
prefetchFirst=false blockTime=10 originLag=149 drift=1792
prefetchFirst=false blockTime=2  originLag=15  drift=184
```

The selector-only model deliberately chooses the event order; it does not itself simulate the full driver. The separate actual-Sequencer probes above establish that the new direct-call path permits that order, while the old path required forkchoice processing before scheduling the next action.

## Downstream impact

With batcher's unchanged `max-channel-duration=100`, a large gap between current L1 head and the last submitted L1 origin causes newly opened channels to expire immediately. We observed single-L2-block channels and a higher number of small L1 submissions while origin lag exceeded that threshold. This appears to be downstream amplification, not the initiating batcher fault.

## Expected behavior / questions

- When the immediate next origin is available, confirmed and timestamp-valid, the new scheduling path should not systematically miss its adoption opportunity because the prefetch event is queued behind the next direct build.
- Can next-origin readiness be established independently of the shared dispatcher, while retaining confirmation-depth, immediate-child, timestamp and max-drift constraints and avoiding unbounded L1 RPC blocking?
- Is there an existing supported mitigation or fix for long-block-time chains that should retain post-Glamsterdam compatibility?

We searched related reports including #11960, #19263, #22821 and the receipts-prefetch changes #22861/#22863, but did not find an exact report of this long-block-time origin-progression regression. Latest stable checked on 2026-10-08 was v1.19.9. Please let us know if this should be linked to an existing issue.

topPRs.title: op-node: prefetch one L1 origin ahead so adoption keeps pace with L1
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Since the sequencer runs on its own goroutine (#22241), it starts each build before the forkchoice update of the previous insertion reaches the L1 origin selector. That update is what prefetches the next origin, so the build finds no next origin cached and keeps the one just adopted. As a result, the L1 origin advances at most once every two L2 blocks.

On chains whose L2 block time exceeds half the L1 block time, this can't keep up with L1. A 10s chain on Sepolia advances one origin per 20s against L1's 12s. Its origin drifts back to the max sequencer drift, about 149 L1 blocks (~30 min) behind the L1 head instead of the confirmation depth. Once the origin has drifted that far, users see:

- deposits included about 30 minutes late
- L1 fee parameters in the L1 block info that are 30 minutes stale
- a sequencer that only advances its origin by a synchronous L1 fetch on the build path, right at the drift limit
- a batcher whose channels exceed `max-channel-duration` immediately, so it posts many single-block batches

Chains with short block times still adopt fast enough and see no change. Operators of affected chains can't work around this by downgrading op-node: on Sepolia, versions without #21920 can no longer follow Glamsterdam L1.

The fix lets the forkchoice handler prefetch one origin further ahead. The block the next build needs is then cached a whole block build earlier, rather than racing the event loop. A lookahead is only promoted if it still extends the new current origin, and the fetch stays off the build path. Behind a confirmation-depth shim, the extra probe costs no L1 RPC in steady state. Without one (`--sequencer.l1-confs=0`), it costs at most one extra by-number call per L2 block.

I rejected two simpler alternatives:
- **Prefetching when the next origin is promoted:** this still adopts only every other block, because the fetch lands one build too late.
- **Fetching synchronously before scheduling the next build:** this puts up to 500ms of L1 RPC back on the hot path that #22241 removed.

`TestOriginSelectorKeepsUpWithL1` reproduces the reported 149-block lag on the old selector and keeps it within the confirmation depth after the fix. The changes to `TestOriginSelectorAdvances` and `TestOriginSelectorHandlesReorg` reflect the new behaviour: the origin no longer waits a block, and a lookahead that a reorg made stale is dropped.

**Review notes.** I ran go-code-reviewer and an adversarial correctness review, and fixed their findings: two lint issues and two comments. I dismissed two low findings; please confirm:
- **A forkchoice update that arrives late clears the origin cache.** If the event loop falls a full block behind the sequencer, that update clears the cache. Clearing costs one hash lookup under the selector's lock and one block on the same origin. This predates this PR and heals itself, so it's left for a follow-up.
- **The next origin is still cached by number without a hash check.** I left it deliberately: an orphaned next origin is what surfaces an L1 reorg as `ErrNextL1OriginOrphaned` and triggers a prompt reset.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23271

topPRs.title: nuts: re-snapshot Lagoon NUT bundle from develop
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Fixes #23097.

## Problem

The Lagoon NUT bundle embedded in op-node and kona-node was snapshotted from `fa9974a2` (2026-05-29) and hasn't been refreshed since. Nine L2 predeploys have been bumped on `develop` since then:

| Contract | Bundle (old) | develop |
|---|---|---|
| SequencerFeeVault, BaseFeeVault, L1FeeVault | 1.6.1 | 1.7.0 |
| OperatorFeeVault | 1.1.1 | 1.2.0 |
| L2ContractsManager | 1.9.1 | 1.14.0 |
| L2DevFeatureFlags | 1.0.0 | 1.3.0 |
| CrossL2Inbox | 1.0.2 | 1.1.0 |
| L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger | 1.3.1 | 1.3.2 |
| ETHLiquidity | 1.1.0 | 1.1.1 |

op-deployer builds genesis from current contracts, so any network with a recent genesis is newer than the bundle. At Lagoon, the L2ProxyAdmin upgrade reverts with `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed(SequencerFeeVault)`. The chain is left with INTEROP enabled but no implementations at `0x…0022/0023/0024`. This is what happened on interop-sdm.

## Change

- `just nut-snapshot-for lagoon` from `develop` @ `bc0d3200`
- `just nut-prefork-state-for lagoon`
- Update the Lagoon L2CM address pinned in `PastNUTBundles.t.sol` (`0x82c0…83c8` → `0x1456…447B`)

The transaction count is unchanged (28).

## Verification

- `packages/contracts-bedrock`: `just generate-nut-bundle` on `develop` produces no diff, so `current-upgrade-bundle.json` was already current and the new Lagoon bundle is byte-identical to it
- `just nut-provenance-verify lagoon`: PASS
- `check-nut-locks`: OK
- **Repro:** a throwaway forge test that runs the *committed* Lagoon bundle on a fresh `CommonTest` genesis. The old bundle fails with `0x1c0a89cc…f8ce5d16…4200…0011`, the same revert as the interop-sdm trace. The new bundle passes.
- `forge test` over `PastNUTBundles` and `L2GenesisForkUpgrade`: 31 passed, 0 failed
- `go test ./op-core/nuts/... ./op-node/rollup/derive/...`: pass
- `cargo test -p kona-hardforks`: pass

## ⚠️ Before merging

Changing an embedded bundle changes the Lagoon activation block. **Any network that has already passed `lagoon_time` on the old bundle would split** once its nodes run a binary with this change. No `lagoon_time` is set in monorepo configs (outside a kona test fixture), but I haven't checked the superchain registry or every devnet. Someone who owns the Lagoon rollout should confirm nothing live depends on the old bundle, and that it wasn't being held frozen on purpose.

## Follow-up (separate PR)

This drift didn't show up in CI because `L2GenesisForkUpgrade` runs a bundle built fresh from source (`buildOutput()`), not the committed `<fork>_nut_bundle.json` that nodes ship. A follow-up can add a test that runs each not-yet-activated fork's committed bundle on a fresh genesis. Running it nightly or on `develop` only would avoid forcing a re-snapshot on every contracts PR.

topPRs.title: docs/ai: make forge op-deployer's only script engine in the op-geth decoupling plan
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Updates the op-geth decoupling plan for `op-chain-ops/script`: instead of building a Rust script engine, op-deployer's existing forge path is extended to every use and the Go host is deleted. Experiments with forge 1.8.3 reproduced the Go host's L1 and L2 genesis state roots exactly, so re-implementing a script engine isn't needed. The plan also drops op-deployer paths that no one uses rather than porting them, and rebuilds the op-e2e interop harness on op-deployer instead of interopgen.

No effect on users; this only changes the plan. The work is tracked in #23300 and its sub-issues, which replace #21743.
